drivers.text: The S&P 500 jumped 4.7% to 7,237 and the Nasdaq rose 6.5%, with Nvidia up 31.5% after its board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. The index move was one of its biggest one-day gains since 1957 and left it above Thursday's close.

drivers.title: CrowdStrike to buy Zscaler, $43.9B
drivers.text: CrowdStrike agreed to buy Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued at about $43.9B, announced with its quarterly results. Zscaler holders get 1.135 CrowdStrike shares each and would own about 15.9% of the combined company.

sowhat.text: A 4.7% rebound and a VIX down to 26.6 reopen the window for stock-funded deals, and CrowdStrike and Zscaler shows strategics will still sign large all-stock transactions. With the 10-year at 4.92% and the Fed meeting on Dec 8-9, financing stays costly, and high yield spreads were wider at 376 bp on Friday.

pitch: Stocks bounced hard on Monday after Friday's rout. The S&P 500 gained 4.7 percent to about 7,240 and the Nasdaq rose 6.5 percent, led by Nvidia, which jumped about 31 percent after its board brought back Jensen Huang as CEO. The VIX fell to about 27. The 10-year was unchanged at 4.92 percent, with the Fed meeting on December 8 and 9. Oil dropped, with WTI down 4.5 percent to about 80 dollars and Brent near 89. On deals, CrowdStrike agreed to buy Zscaler for about 44 billion dollars in an all-stock deal.

quiz.q: Where did WTI crude settle on Mon 23 Nov?
Why did the Nasdaq rise 6.5% on 23 Nov?
quiz.a: A chip-led rebound: Nvidia rose 31.5% after its board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, recovering Friday's losses.

quiz.q: What is CrowdStrike paying for Zscaler, and in what form?
quiz.a: About $43.9B in an all-stock deal, 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per Zscaler share.

chat.a: Monday was a sharp rebound: the S&P 500 rose 4.7% to 7,237 and the Nasdaq 6.5%, after Friday's AI-led rout. Nvidia rose 31.5% after its board reinstated Jensen Huang. The VIX fell to 26.62, and the 10-year held at 4.92%.
chat.tip: Lead with the rebound, then say the 10-year did not move.

chat.q: What's your read on oil this week?
chat.a: WTI settled at $80.17, down 4.5%, and Brent at $89.37, down 3.5%, a spread of about $9. Gas also fell 6.7% to $3.184. Lower prices ease the pressure on consumers but can widen buyer-seller valuation gaps in energy M&A.
chat.tip: Give the level and the direction, then stop.

chat.a: CrowdStrike agreed to buy Zscaler for about $43.9B in stock, with Zscaler holders owning about 15.9% of the combined company. In power, Archrock is buying HiVolt Energy for up to $450M, with Evercore advising Archrock and BofA Securities advising HiVolt.
chat.tip: Name the advisers on the energy deal; bankers will ask.

chat.q: What are you watching over the next few weeks?
chat.a: The Dec 8-9 FOMC, with the 10-year at 4.92% and the funds rate at 3.75-4.00%. I am also watching whether the rebound holds after the Thanksgiving break, since the S&P was more than 10% below its record on Friday.
chat.tip: Tie each event to financing conditions.

chat.q: Why do all-stock deals like CrowdStrike and Zscaler get done in a volatile market?
chat.a: In an all-stock deal both sides share the price move, so a swing in CrowdStrike's shares changes the value but not the ratio of 1.135 shares per Zscaler share. It also avoids new debt when the 10-year is 4.92%. The risk is that the offer value floats, and Zscaler traded about 3.3% below the offer at Monday's close.
chat.tip: Say fixed exchange ratio, floating value.

chat.q: If the 10-year rose 50 bp, what happens to a DCF?
chat.a: The 10-year is 4.92% now. A 50 bp rise lifts the risk-free rate and so the WACC, which lowers the present value of cash flows. Long-duration assets with most of their value in the terminal value are hit hardest.
chat.tip: Say the direction, then who is hit hardest.

chat.q: How would you describe credit markets right now?
chat.a: Spreads widened on Friday: high yield at 376 bp, up 24 bp, and investment grade at 98 bp, up 4 bp. That is still a functioning market, but the Monday reading is not yet published, so I would watch whether the equity rebound pulls spreads back in. For sponsors, wider spreads raise the cost of leveraged buyouts.
